concepts.def: Behaviour breaking the formal laws of a society and punishable by the state; varies across time and place.
Behaviour breaking informal norms but not always laws; relative to time, place and audience.
Durkheim (1895): crime is inevitable and functional; boundary maintenance, social change, adaptation.
Merton (1938): blocked legitimate routes to success cause innovation (crime); also retreatism, ritualism, rebellion, conformity.
Becker (1963) Outsiders: deviance results from successful application of a label rather than the act itself.
Crime is a product of capitalist inequality; selective enforcement targets working-class crimes over corporate harm.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Sociology of Crime & Deviance — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Sociology of Crime & Deviance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Sociology of Crime & Deviance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Labelling theory was developed by Becker in:
What is Young and Willmott's symmetrical family thesis?
options: That modern families have moved toward more shared, joint roles between partners — domestic and economic responsibilities increasingly shared, in contrast to segregated traditional roles.
The symmetrical family means men and women now do exactly equal amounts of housework.
Material deprivation is about a lack of clothing; cultural deprivation is about not visiting museums.
The symmetrical family means families with the same number of boys and girls.
Ethnocentrism is the same as racism.
Ethnocentrism means concentrating on your own ethnic group only.

Judging other cultures by the standards of one's own — assuming one's own cultural practices and values are normal or superior. It is a methodological problem in social research as well as a social phenomenon.
Material deprivation is about a lack of clothing; cultural deprivation is about not visiting museums.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between material and cultural deprivation?
options: Material deprivation refers to lack of physical/economic resources (housing, books, food); cultural deprivation refers to lack of skills, values and norms (e.g. parental attitudes to education) that are claimed to support achievement.
Ethnocentrism means concentrating on your own ethnic group only.
Material deprivation is about a lack of clothing; cultural deprivation is about not visiting museums.
Material and cultural deprivation are two names for the same poverty.
